maria.g: Quick share — ran a focused benchmark comparing synthetic steady-rate traffic vs recorded-trace replay for /rerank (embed -> dot-product). p50/p95 look fine both ways but replay has consistent 99.9th spikes. attaching run summary and asking if this is likely kernel selection or KV cache behavior.

jonathan: Can you paste the exact bench flags? e.g., batch caps, kv cache on/off, kernel mode?

maria.g: Sure — ran three sweeps. Commands:
```
./rerank_bench --mode=synthetic --qps=800 --batch_cap=64 --kv_cache=on --kernel=auto
./rerank_bench --mode=replay --trace=prod_trace_03 --batch_cap=64 --kv_cache=on --kernel=auto
./rerank_bench --mode=replay --trace=prod_trace_03 --batch_cap=64 --kv_cache=off --kernel=auto
```
Key numbers for vector_dim=512, payload ~3kb:
- synthetic (kv=on): p50=22ms p95=48ms p99=76ms p99.9=120ms
- replay (kv=on): p50=23ms p95=55ms p99=220ms p99.9=920ms
- replay (kv=off): p50=25ms p95=60ms p99=240ms p99.9=950ms
So turning kv_cache off didn't remove the tail. kernel=auto picks different kernels across iterations (we log selection).

anya: Interesting. Two quick hypotheses: 1) replay arrival pattern creates microbursts that push batch formation to a different regime (big batch variance => different kernel chosen or memory pressure), 2) KV cache eviction/hits at the moment of a microburst. Do you have batch-size distribution and kv_hit_ratio over time?

maria.g: I dumped some logs. batch_size distribution (replay): [1: 18%, 2-8: 42%, 9-32: 28%, 33-64: 12%] — median batch=6, mean=11. kv_hit_ratio hovers ~87% but dips to ~52% during the big p99 events. snippet: 
```
[10:12:33] batch=48 kernel=matmul_large p99_event=true kv_hit=0.53 mem_free=2.1GB
[10:12:34] batch=2 kernel=matmul_small p99_event=false kv_hit=0.89 mem_free=3.8GB
```
Looks like kernel switches mid-burst.

chip: That batch distribution screams bursty arrival. Auto kernel selection probably flips between small/big-batch kernels; the cost of switching (memory layout, cold caches) + partial KV misses could explain the big tails. Also check whether the runtime is moving between quantized/unquantized code paths.

jonathan: Can you run with explicit kernel pinning for a repro? e.g., force matmul_small versus matmul_large and compare p99. Also try arrival-smoothing in the harness: a token bucket to smooth microbursts. If p99 drops with smoothing, it's arrival pattern, not model weight issue.

kris: Another actionable: enable continuous KV-prefix caching (we have a flag --prefetch-kv) so that when a large batch arrives we avoid cache misses. Also log TLB/PCIe stalls around the p99 events (if possible).

maria.g: Re-ran two quick variants: 1) replay + kernel=matmul_small + prefetch-kv on 2) replay + kernel=matmul_large + prefetch-kv on. Results (p99.9):
- small kernel + prefetch: 210ms
- large kernel + prefetch: 230ms
Both much lower than 920ms but still higher than synthetic baseline. So prefetch helps a lot.

perf-bot: [bench-run] 1819521200 - /rerank replay trace=prod_trace_03 kv_prefetch=on kernel=matmul_small p99.9=210ms link=https://artifacts/bench/1819521200

anya: Nice. That points to a combination of cache warmup + burst semantics. For a follow-up I'd suggest: 1) log kernel switch latency (time to rebind kernels), 2) histogram of kv_hit by batch_size, 3) run per-shard mem pressure metrics.

chip: Also consider a small runtime change: add a hysteresis window to kernel selector (only change kernel if mean batch over last N windows crosses threshold). That reduces oscillation during bursts.

maria.g: Agree. Plan of action:
- implement arrival smoothing in harness and re-run replay (to get apples-to-apples vs synthetic)
- pin kernel for a controlled run + collect kernel-flip timing
- enable detailed mem/tlb counters during next run
- instrument kv_hit by request age (to see prefix eviction correlation)
I'll post results later today. thanks all :thumbsup:

kris: If you want, I can spin a dedicated small pool to remove neighbor-noise and isolate runtime behavior.

maria.g: That would be great — request sent to eng-runtime infra.

jonathan: also add vector_dim=256 sweep to see dim sensitivity (earlier we saw smaller dims reduce p99 in some kernels).

maria.g: yup adding that to the matrix. will update thread with final numbers.
